scenario.name: Microsoft MSRC & Dirk-jan Mollema DFIR — Entra ID Primary Refresh Token (PRT) & Rogue Device Registration Forensics
scenario.overview: Imagine a lively downtown city street intersection with painted zebra crosswalks, glowing red-yellow-green traffic lights, corner shop awnings, and passing yellow taxis. At the busy downtown street corner, an impostor wearing a reflective utility vest kneels beside the metal traffic-signal control cabinet while pedestrians cross the street. In this real-world scenario, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the traffic officer's station, then quietly copies a trusted access pass from the traffic officer's station. The city intersection camera and municipal traffic control board detect the impossible all-green light timing and dispatch a traffic officer immediately. In this scenario (T1528, Microsoft MSRC & Dirk-jan Mollema DFIR, Entra ID Primary Refresh Token , PRT & Rogue Device Registration Forensics), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: token Acquisition for Device Registration, then rogue Device Registration in Entra ID, then primary Refresh Token Sign-In. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Token Acquisition for Device Registration, then Rogue Device Registration in Entra ID, then Primary Refresh Token Sign-In, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on Azure AD Event 100 correlated across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: Stage 3: Primary Refresh Token (PRT) Sign-In & Persistent Session Key Forensics (IncomingTokenType=primaryRefreshToken)
stages.subtitle: Defense Evasion (T1550.001 - Primary Refresh Token Persistence Across Password Reset)
stages.description: Traffic signals flip out of rhythm across the city intersection, creating instant confusion that lets an unmarked courier slip past the corner storefront unseen. In this final step inside the city street, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the traffic officer's station until the intersection traffic camera catches the mismatch. Using the registered device certificate and software session key, the actor requests a Primary Refresh Token (PRT) valid for 14 days (renewable for 90 days) that persists across user password changes until the device object itself is disabled or deleted in Entra ID. Subsequent sign-ins show IncomingTokenType="primaryRefreshToken" and DeviceDetail.deviceId="d4819c02-..." (logged in Network Event 200 with LogCategory=Entra ID SignInLogs, IncomingTokenType=primaryRefreshToken , PRT, DeviceId=d4819c02-5511-4a90-8111-223344556677, IrRemediation=Disable/delete rogue DeviceId + Revoke-MgUserSignInSession so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Next, the follow-up artifact Remediation: Set-MgDevice -DeviceId d4819c02-... -AccountEnabled:$false; Revoke-MgUserSignInSession runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , Remediation: Set-MgDevice -DeviceId d4819c02-... -AccountEnabled:$false; Revoke-MgUserSignIn so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1550.001 during "Primary Refresh Token , PRT Sign-In & Persistent Session Key Forensics , IncomingTokenType=primaryRefreshToken" , Using the registered device certificate and software session key, the actor requests a Primary Refresh Token , PRT valid for 14 days , renewable for 90 days that persists across user password changes until the device object itself is disabled or deleted in Entra ID while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ Entra SignInLogs: IncomingTokenType=primaryRefreshToken from DeviceId d4819c02-... / ⇠#3 RESP 200) from Node ③ (#3 Entra ID DRS Service) to Node ④ (#4 Registered Device Object), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 PRT Sign-In (IncomingToken PRT)).

steps.plainTitle: Primary Refresh Token (PRT) Sign-In & Persistent Session Key Forensics (IncomingTokenType=primaryRefreshToken)
steps.storyAnalogy: Traffic signals flip out of rhythm across the city intersection, creating instant confusion that lets an unmarked courier slip past the corner storefront unseen. In this final step inside the city street, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the traffic officer's station until the intersection traffic camera catches the mismatch.
steps.simpleExplanation: Using the registered device certificate and software session key, the actor requests a Primary Refresh Token (PRT) valid for 14 days (renewable for 90 days) that persists across user password changes until the device object itself is disabled or deleted in Entra ID. Subsequent sign-ins show IncomingTokenType="primaryRefreshToken" and DeviceDetail.deviceId="d4819c02-..."
